headline: Shares of CoreWeave and other AI cloud rental companies fell sharply after Gartner forecast that most of them will not survive as independent businesses beyond 2030.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a market-moving forecast, but it is one firm's prediction.
importance_line: Investors in AI infrastructure companies and the businesses that rent their computing power are affected, and the finding is a forecast from one research firm that depends on spending continuing at its current pace.
summary: Seeking Alpha reports that CoreWeave fell 15 percent by noon on 14 Oct 2026 and DigitalOcean 14 percent after research firm Gartner predicted that more than 80 percent of "neoclouds", companies that rent out AI computing power, will not remain independent much beyond 2030 if spending continues at its pace. Gartner says AI data center owners would need $8.5 trillion of revenue by 2030 to cover their costs and a 12 percent return but are forecast to earn only $3.6 trillion, and sees Amazon, Google and Microsoft as better placed to survive.
notes: Read via TradingView, which carries the Seeking Alpha article; Gartner analyst Will Sommer is also spelled 'Somner' once in the text.
